findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a post-rollback-state assertion for the DC (lossy) path: after the cutover flag is flipped OFF, a plain/identity re-push from the intact rebar Markdown source restores the affected Jira bodies (assert the recovered state, not merely that the wire behavior reverted), or attach a `DATA LOSS RISK` note if the lossy Jira bodies are not recoverable.
evidence: Design: 'DC is a one-way Markdown→wiki renderer'; 'Jira wiki markup is lossy for punctuation-dense prose'.
Plan rollback AC asserts the wire 'reverts to the plain/identity wire when off' — a behavior assertion, not a post-rollback body-state assertion.

POST-ROLLBACK STATE applicability: the plan performs a one-way (lossy) transformation and reinterprets existing persisted bodies, so it must assert state AFTER rollback, not merely that rollback completed.
findings.finding: Rollback for the DC path is a flag flip that 'restores the plain/identity path', and the DC render is explicitly one-way and LOSSY, yet the rollback AC asserts only that the wire behavior reverts (test_cutover_rollback_restores_plain), not the post-rollback STATE of bodies already rewritten to lossy rendered wiki on Jira. The plan does not assert that a post-rollback plain/identity re-push from the intact rebar Markdown source restores those bodies.
findings.location: disparaged-parodistic-shrew (3388) — 'Rollback' bullet and rollback AC ('reverts to the plain/identity wire when off; verified by ... test_cutover_rollback_restores_plain')
scenarios: A DC tenant is cut over, descriptions on Jira are rewritten to lossy rendered wiki, then a bad rollout triggers rollback; an operator needs assurance the lossy Jira bodies are restored to their intended form (from rebar's intact Markdown source) on the next plain-path pass, not left as the lossy rendered artifact.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion verifying the plain/identity rollback flag reverts both Cloud and DC send paths to prior behavior.
evidence: "flag-gated rollback" (Sequencing)
"Preserve the plain/identity flag rollback." (Live cutover plus echo suppression)
No AC exercises the rollback flag returning to plain-text/identity behavior.
findings.finding: The plan repeatedly describes a flag-gated rollback (plain/identity codec fallback) as a first-class safety mechanism, but no acceptance criterion verifies the rollback path works.
findings.location: Design / Sequencing / Live cutover; Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: Cutover misbehaves in production; operators toggle the rollback flag but its behavior was never validated in-session.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a cross-platform subprocess-termination strategy for the pandoc timeout path so the identity fallback works on Windows, not only via POSIX process-group kill.
evidence: Plan quote: 'Bound subprocess work per field. Kill the process group on timeout.'
POSIX-only fact: os.killpg / start_new_session process-group kill is not available on Windows; CreateProcess groups behave differently and Python's os.killpg raises AttributeError on Windows.
findings.finding: The DC robustness step specifies 'Kill the process group on timeout', which relies on POSIX process-group semantics (os.killpg / SIGKILL to a pgid). Windows has no equivalent process-group kill, so the timeout-recovery path cannot execute as written on a Windows platform.
findings.location: Child responsibilities → DC robustness: 'Kill the process group on timeout'
scenarios: Platform=Windows developer workstation or CI: a pandoc subprocess that exceeds dc_pandoc_timeout_s cannot be group-killed; the timeout handler raises AttributeError/OSError instead of terminating the process, leaving an orphaned pandoc and no clean identity fallback.
findings.suggested_fix: State an OS-conditional termination approach (e.g. CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP + terminate() on Windows, killpg on POSIX) or use a portable subprocess helper, and add the guarantee that timeout fallback is exercised on all supported platforms.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the two-asymmetric-codec + echo-safety architectural decision (and the wiki-lossiness rationale) in an ADR or design-doc update.
evidence: Plan quote: 'Use two asymmetric codecs behind one state-based echo-safety layer on the existing adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py seam.'
Only ADR reference is to the existing ADR-0026 baseline; no new architectural-decision record is proposed for the asymmetric (bidirectional Cloud vs one-way DC) codec design.
findings.finding: The design introduces a novel two-asymmetric-codec architecture plus a state-based echo-safety layer, but only cites the pre-existing ADR-0026 baseline. No new ADR or design-doc capture is planned for the new asymmetric-codec / origin-gating / three-way-comparison decision.
findings.location: Design section: 'Use two asymmetric codecs behind one state-based echo-safety layer'
scenarios: Future maintainer encounters the deliberate Cloud-bidirectional / DC-one-way asymmetry and the lossy-wiki rationale with no recorded decision, risking an attempt to 'fix' DC into a fixed-point codec.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a child task or acceptance note to record a new ADR documenting why Cloud is bidirectional while DC is one-way render, referencing the corpus experiments.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the live Cloud path handles the ~0.35% of bodies that are NOT Markdown↔ADF fixed points (e.g. change-gate the outbound emit on the rich_sha of the RENDERED wire rather than on a decode-equality compare, or pin the baseline to the observed-after-push canonical value) so non-idempotent bodies converge instead of re-emitting every pass.
evidence: Design: 'marklas reached 99.65% idempotent Markdown↔ADF round-trip over that corpus.'

outbound_field_diff.py:449-457 and the once-only re-emit compare (outbound_fields.py:555-561) converge only when normalize_outbound(t) is a fixed point; for a non-idempotent body normalize_outbound(local) never equals the decoded remote, so the emit fires each pass.
0.35% of 5,730 bodies is ~20 bodies that would churn indefinitely, contradicting the 'zero committed-state entries' AC for those tickets.
findings.finding: The echo-suppression / once-only re-emit convergence mechanism silently assumes Cloud Markdown↔ADF round-trip is a fixed point, but the plan itself reports only 99.65% idempotency — the residual ~0.35% of bodies never reach a fixed point, so their decode-on-compare never converges and they re-emit a description update on every reconcile pass. The plan does not specify how the non-idempotent residue is handled on the live path.
findings.location: Design ('marklas reached 99.65% idempotent Markdown↔ADF round-trip'); AC 'The Cloud corpus reaches an idempotent Markdown↔ADF fixed point' and 'An unchanged reconcile pass adds zero committed-state entries attributable to rich-text sync'
scenarios: A Cloud description in the non-idempotent 0.35% is synced; every subsequent no-op reconcile pass re-emits a description update and advances a committed-state entry, producing perpetual churn.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define whether 789c's comment rendering is gated by 3388's per-client cutover flag (so comment and description rendering flip together per client) and state it in 789c, so AC2/AC5 are satisfied by the production path under the flag-on state and comment rendering never diverges from the description cutover state.
evidence: 789c: 'Outbound comment bodies are rendered through the SAME RichTextCodec.to_wire seam ... (AdfCodec.to_wire for Cloud, the now-rendering WikiTextCodec.to_wire for DC after 3388)'
3388 AC: 'The cutover is flag-gated, ships defaulting OFF (opt-in per-client, not a 100%-traffic flip), and reverts to the plain/identity wire when off'
789c has no mention of the cutover flag / gating on the comment path in its Approach, Scope, or ACs
findings.finding: 789c routes outbound comment bodies through AdfCodec.to_wire / WikiTextCodec.to_wire to satisfy parent AC2 (Cloud comment -> structured ADF) and AC5 (DC comment -> rendered wiki), but 3388 ships the rich cutover flag DEFAULTING OFF (opt-in per client), and when that flag is OFF the codec ops revert to the plain/identity pass-through. 789c never references the cutover flag on the comment path, so it assumes to_wire renders rich unconditionally, which contradicts 3388's flag-off default.
scenarios: With the rich cutover flag OFF (the shipped default) for a client, 789c's comment path calls AdfCodec.to_wire which is the plain pass-through, so comments encode as plain-text ADF, not structured ADF — parent AC2/AC5 (structured ADF / rendered wiki through the production comment path) is not met while the flag is off, and there is no defined toggle for comment rendering.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to 789c an explicit statement that the comment to_wire rendering is gated by the same per-client cutover flag 3388 introduces (comments render rich only when the client's cutover is enabled), and add a test asserting comment encoding follows the flag state.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the one-time legacy-body upgrade re-emit is throttled/batched per tenant at cutover (e.g. rate cap or per-pass cap on re-emitted bodies) so the corpus-wide upgrade burst cannot trip Jira API rate limits or stall a partial upgrade.
evidence: Plan: 'Each already-synced description re-emits exactly once ... to upgrade to rich ADF, then converges.'
Design corpus scale: '1,801 tickets / 5,730 bodies'
ABSENCE: no mention of batching, throttling, or Jira API rate-limit handling for the one-time re-emit burst; the flag gating addresses opt-in/canary but not write-rate.
T11(b): large backfills are batched/throttled, not one giant burst.
findings.finding: The one-time 'legacy-body upgrade re-emit' is a corpus-wide backfill of Jira writes at cutover (one rendered-body push per already-synced description across ~5,730 bodies), but the plan specifies no throttling/batching of that write burst against the Jira API. The OFF-by-default flag and per-client canary limit blast radius but do not bound the per-tenant re-emit rate once enabled.
findings.location: disparaged-parodistic-shrew (3388) — 'The live cutover' / 'Rich-aware compare' (once-only re-emit); Design 'grounded in six experiments over ... 1,801 tickets / 5,730 bodies'
scenarios: A tenant with thousands of already-synced descriptions has the cutover flag enabled; the next reconcile pass attempts to re-emit every legacy body at once and hits Jira API rate limits or 429s, partially applying the upgrade and stalling.
A canary validates convergence on a small ticket set but the production tenant's re-emit volume overwhelms the write path.
